blocks.html: Chapters 2 and 3 reduced a dataset to a few numbers: a centre, a spread, a shape. A picture often shows what those numbers hide. Two variables can share the same mean, SD and skewness while a histogram shows that one of them has two peaks, perhaps because two subpopulations were mixed. This chapter covers tables (§4.1), diagrams for categorical data (§4.2), diagrams for the distribution of a numeric variable (§4.3), the scatter diagram for two numeric variables (§4.4), and the diagrams community medicine uses for time, place and population (§4.5). The chart you pick follows from the variable’s scale of measurement (recall §1.1.2) and from the question you want the reader to answer.
